title: Adaptive HACT: Information Limits and Safe Adaptation of Verification Evidence
abstract: Adaptive verification evidence raises two questions: which completion statistics identify an efficient representation, and how may that representation change without weakening acceptance? Adaptive HACT (Hyperedge-Aware Certificate Trees) separates a protected semantic registry from generation-fenced certificate trees and prices packets touched by joint completion sets. We prove that exact singleton and pairwise probabilities can leave globally optimal trees unidentified for every fanout of at least three and every affine positive-slot packet price, with sharp minimax regret. A complete-epoch construction extends this limitation to fixed-eight batching within a two-layout class. Under exchangeable complete batches, a specialization of established tree optimization provides an exact global baseline. A local publication invariant preserves acceptance through migration; a conditional adoption rule includes calibration, shift and installation costs. Independent enumeration checks 74,245 tree comparisons. Retrospective scoring finds that the symmetric baseline beats frozen full-wave refinement on all 15 item-shuffled traces and loses on all 15 file-group traces. It costs 21.26–62.13% more on original holdouts. Without byte observers, the tree service takes 1.61–3.54 times the maintained-counter ledger's operation time. The results establish information limits and conditional adaptation guarantees; service and agent speedups remain unproven.
